- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–5% buffer below forecast for early drops.
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap next-day forecast at 10% below peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.0 to 1.0 in 3–5 days), model overreacts; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period reversals; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment turns negative or volatility spikes.
